headings.title: Applicability to offenses committed after July 1, 1984
headings.reviewNote: Governs construction, charging, trial, punishment, and appellate review of chapter offenses committed after July 1, 1984.

headings.title: Inapplicability to prior offenses and preservation of prior law
headings.reviewNote: Excludes offenses committed before the chapter's effective date and preserves prior governing law notwithstanding section 1.160.

headings.title: Application of criminal code and controlling effect upon conflict
headings.reviewNote: Applies consistent provisions of The Criminal Code or other law and establishes that this chapter controls in conflicts.

headings.title: Venue and county of prosecution for homicide offenses
headings.reviewNote: Specifies prosecution venue rules for homicide offenses based on offense location, elements, victim's body discovery, or victim residence.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and effective date 10-01-84 (note subsection 1 text references offenses committed after July 1, 1984); post-1984 applicability, prior-law preservation notwithstanding section 1.160, code conflict rule, and four-tier homicide venue verified.

headings.title: Transferred intent and unidentified victim provisions
headings.reviewNote: Governs transferred intent when a different person is killed and bars defense based on inability to establish the intended victim's identity.

headings.title: Time elapsed between conduct and death no defense
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the length of time between conduct and resulting death does not constitute a defense to a homicide charge.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and 2023 S.B. 227 amendment; transferred intent including unidentified intended victims and non-defense of elapsed time between conduct and death verified.

headings.title: Separate counts, joinder restrictions, and submission of lesser offenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate counts for lawfully joined offenses, limits joinder with first degree murder, and requires submission of supported offenses and lesser offenses upon request.

headings.title: Joinder of alternative counts without election requirement
headings.reviewNote: Permits joining alternative homicide or non-homicide counts regarding a single victim without requiring state election, preserving certain conjunctive trials.

headings.title: Joinder with first degree murder for prior offenders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes joint trial of first degree murder and non-murder counts when prior offender status makes judicial sentencing applicable to the non-murder charge.

headings.title: Joinder authorized upon state waiver of death penalty
headings.reviewNote: Permits trying and submitting first degree murder with other lawfully joined charges when the state waives the death penalty.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, effective date 1-01-17, and 1989 Bulloch v. Seier annotation; separate counts, first-degree murder joinder limits, alternative counts without election, prior-offender joinder, and death-penalty waiver joinder verified.

headings.title: Pretrial disclosure of penalty-phase evidence and witnesses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates reciprocal pretrial disclosure of penalty-phase aggravating and mitigating circumstances, witnesses, and exhibits upon request in capital trials.

headings.title: Supplemental relation to supreme court discovery rules
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory penalty-phase disclosures supplement supreme court discovery rules, protective orders, and sanctions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 10-01-84; reciprocal capital penalty-phase disclosure of section 565.032 circumstances, witnesses, and exhibits and supplemental relation to supreme court discovery rules verified.

headings.title: Pretrial waiver of jury trial with court assent
headings.reviewNote: Permits defendant to waive jury trial on all issues and punishment with court assent prior to trial commencement.

headings.title: Jury punishment trial barred after guilty plea or bench trial
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits jury trial on punishment following a guilty plea or bench trial conviction for homicide unless the state agrees.

headings.title: Jury punishment waiver restriction in capital cases
headings.reviewNote: Bars defendant from waiving a jury for capital penalty phase following a jury guilt verdict unless state and court agree.

headings.title: Entry of jury waiver and agreement in court record
headings.reviewNote: Requires any permitted jury trial waiver and agreement to be entered in the court record.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, effective date 10-01-84, and 2002 Ring v. Arizona Sixth Amendment annotation; pretrial jury waiver with court assent, restrictions after plea/bench/capital jury verdict, and record entry verified.

headings.title: Conditions where consent constitutes a defense to physical injury
headings.reviewNote: Establishes limited conditions under which victim consent is a defense to conduct causing or threatening physical injury.

headings.title: Burden of injecting the issue of consent on defendant
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of injecting the issue of consent upon the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, transfer note (formerly 565.080), and effective date 1-01-17; three limited consent defenses to physical injury (including chapter 563 justification) and defendant burden to inject verified.

headings.title: Elements of murder in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of murder in the first degree as knowingly causing the death of another person after deliberation.

headings.title: Classification and authorized punishments by age
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree murder as a class A felony, specifying death or life without parole for adults and section 565.033 penalties for juveniles under eighteen.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, effective date 7-13-16, and section 546.730 cross-reference; first-degree murder elements and class A felony punishments by age (death/LWOP for 18+ vs section 565.033 for under 18) verified.

headings.title: Elements of conventional and felony murder in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines second degree murder elements for knowingly causing death, causing death with purpose of serious physical injury, and felony murder during felony perpetration or immediate flight.

headings.title: Classification and cumulative punishment with related felonies
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second degree murder as a class A felony and mandates punishment in addition to related non-homicide felonies.

headings.title: Consideration of supported alternative theories upon request
headings.reviewNote: Requires instructing or considering all evidentially supported second degree murder statutory theories upon request of a party or the court.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, effective date 1-01-17, section 544.671 cross-reference, and 2 case annotations (Searcy, Pembleton); refined subsection 1 note to 'knowingly causing death' and verified cumulative felony punishment and alternative-theory submission.

headings.title: Elements of voluntary manslaughter and assisted self-murder
headings.reviewNote: Defines voluntary manslaughter as second degree murder committed under sudden passion arising from adequate cause or knowingly assisting self-murder.

headings.title: Burden of injecting sudden passion on defendant
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of injecting the issue of sudden passion arising from adequate cause upon the defendant.

headings.title: Class B felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies voluntary manslaughter as a class B felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; voluntary manslaughter (sudden passion or knowingly assisting self-murder), defendant burden to inject sudden passion, and class B felony classification verified.

headings.title: Elements of involuntary manslaughter in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines involuntary manslaughter in the first degree as recklessly causing the death of another person.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for targeting law enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree involuntary manslaughter as a class C felony, enhanced to class B if targeting a law enforcement officer or second-degree relative.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and 2 case annotations (State v. Knapp, Fields v. Mo. Bd. of Probation & Parole); reckless first-degree involuntary manslaughter and class C/class B law-enforcement targeting enhancement verified.

headings.title: Elements of involuntary manslaughter in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines involuntary manslaughter in the second degree as causing the death of any person with criminal negligence.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for targeting law enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second degree involuntary manslaughter as a class E felony, enhanced to class D if targeting a law enforcement officer or second-degree relative.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; criminal-negligence second-degree involuntary manslaughter and class E/class D law-enforcement targeting enhancement verified.

headings.title: General application of section 556.046 to homicide cases
headings.reviewNote: Directs the use of section 556.046 for considering lesser offenses in homicide cases, subject to statutory exceptions.

headings.title: Hierarchical lists of lesser degree homicide offenses
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates the hierarchical order of lesser degree offenses for first degree murder and second degree murder charges.

headings.title: Request required for submitting lesser included offense instruction
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits submitting instructions on lesser included offenses unless requested by a party or the court.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, transfer note (formerly 565.025), and effective date 1-01-17; section 556.046 applicability, hierarchical lesser-degree homicide lists, and party/court request requirement verified.

headings.title: Proceedings when capital punishment not submitted or waived
headings.reviewNote: Governs proceedings when first degree murder is not submitted or the state waives the death penalty, proceeding as standard criminal cases.

headings.title: Bifurcated trial procedure and non-capital count sentencing
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a two-stage capital trial procedure before the same trier and provides for judicial sentencing on joined non-capital offenses for prior offenders.

headings.title: Second stage proceedings upon conviction of lesser homicide
headings.reviewNote: Outlines second stage punishment argument and declaration when the capital trier finds the defendant guilty of a lesser homicide offense.

headings.title: Capital penalty phase evidence, findings, and sentencing standards
headings.reviewNote: Governs evidence, argument, findings on intellectual disability and aggravating/mitigating factors, and jury instructions when determining life without parole or death.

headings.title: Pretrial determination of intellectual disability by agreement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pretrial court determination of intellectual disability upon written agreement of parties and leave of court without prejudicing jury submission.

headings.title: Definition of intellectual disability
headings.reviewNote: Defines intellectual disability based on subaverage intellectual functioning, adaptive deficits in two or more behaviors, and onset documented before age eighteen.

headings.title: Applicability to offenses committed on or after August 28, 2001
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the application of the section's provisions to offenses committed on or after August 28, 2001.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 7 subsections and 2003 State v. Whitfield annotation (jury deadlock judicial four-step sentencing violates Ring v. Arizona); bifurcated capital procedure, four-step penalty standards, intellectual disability determination/definition, and August 28, 2001 applicability verified.

headings.title: Trier considerations and jury instructions on aggravating circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required trier considerations regarding statutory aggravating circumstances and overall aggravating and mitigating evidence in capital sentencing.

headings.title: Statutory aggravating circumstances for first degree murder
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates the exclusive statutory aggravating circumstances authorized for consideration in first degree murder penalty proceedings.

headings.title: Statutory mitigating circumstances for first degree murder
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory mitigating circumstances for consideration in first degree murder penalty proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; trier considerations/jury instructions, 17 exclusive statutory aggravating circumstances, and 7 statutory mitigating circumstances verified.

headings.title: Authorized sentences for juvenile first degree murder offenders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sentences of life without parole under section 565.034, life with parole, or thirty to forty years for offenders under age eighteen.

headings.title: Mandatory sentencing factors for juvenile first degree murder offenders
headings.reviewNote: Sets out mandatory mitigating and offender-specific factors that the judge or jury must consider when sentencing juvenile first degree murder offenders.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 7-13-16; authorized juvenile first-degree murder sentences (LWOP under section 565.034, life with parole, or 30–40 years) and 10 mandatory youth sentencing factors verified.

headings.title: Written notice of intent to seek juvenile life without parole
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice of intent to seek life without parole for a juvenile offender within 120 days of arraignment, listing aggravating factors.

headings.title: Extension of motion filing deadline upon notice
headings.reviewNote: Grants defendant an additional sixty days to file new motions or supplement pending motions after notice of intent is filed.

headings.title: Withdrawal of notice of intent and prohibition against refiling
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes withdrawal of notice of intent by written notice and prohibits refiling once withdrawn.

headings.title: Bifurcated trial requirement following notice of intent
headings.reviewNote: Mandates a two-stage trial before the same trier when notice of intent is filed, reserving punishment determination for the second stage.

headings.title: Second stage sentencing proceeding upon first degree murder conviction
headings.reviewNote: Provides for a second stage punishment proceeding following a first-stage conviction of murder in the first degree.

headings.title: Eligibility criteria and aggravating factors for juvenile life without parole
headings.reviewNote: Conditions juvenile life without parole eligibility on beyond-a-reasonable-doubt findings of personal infliction of fatal injuries and an enumerated aggravating factor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 6 subsections and effective date 7-13-16; 120-day written LWOP notice, 60-day defense motion extension, non-refilable withdrawal, bifurcated trial, and beyond-a-reasonable-doubt personal-infliction plus aggravating-factor eligibility verified.

headings.title: Mandatory supreme court sentence review and trial record transmission
headings.reviewNote: Mandates supreme court review of death sentences upon final judgment and requires clerk transmission of record and standard judge questionnaire within ten days.

headings.title: Consideration of punishment and enumerated appellate errors
headings.reviewNote: Directs supreme court to review both the imposed death sentence and any errors raised on appeal.

headings.title: Statutory determinations required in capital sentence review
headings.reviewNote: Defines required supreme court determinations regarding arbitrary factors, evidentiary support for aggravating circumstances, and sentence proportionality.

headings.title: Right to submit briefs and present oral argument
headings.reviewNote: Establishes rights of both defendant and state to file briefs and deliver oral argument during sentence review.

headings.title: Case comparisons and authorized supreme court dispositions
headings.reviewNote: Requires reference to similar cases and authorizes supreme court to affirm death sentence, resentence to life without parole, or remand for punishment retrial.

headings.title: Supreme court assistant, case record accumulation, and staff
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes appointment of supreme court assistant attorney, accumulation of capital and life without parole case records, and staff support.

headings.title: Direct appeal of conviction and consolidation with sentence review
headings.reviewNote: Provides for waivable direct appeal of conviction to supreme court and consolidation of appeal with mandatory sentence review.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 7 subsections, effective date 1-01-17, and 1995 Oxford v. Delo annotation; mandatory supreme court death-sentence review, 10-day record transmission, three statutory determinations, dispositions, supreme court assistant, and consolidated direct appeal verified.

headings.title: Resentencing to life without parole if death penalty held unconstitutional
headings.reviewNote: Mandates judicial resentencing to life without parole if the death penalty is held unconstitutional, reserving remand authority for invalid aggravating factors.

headings.title: Trial court resentencing procedure when specific death sentence held unconstitutional
headings.reviewNote: Requires trial court to bring defendant before the court and impose life without parole if a death sentence is held unconstitutional, with remand exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; fallback life-without-parole resentencing if death penalty or a specific death sentence is held unconstitutional, preserving section 565.035(5) remand authority for invalid aggravating factors, verified.

headings.reviewNote: Defines first degree assault as attempting to kill or knowingly causing or attempting to cause serious physical injury to another.

headings.title: Classification and enhancements for injury or special victim
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree assault as a class B felony, enhanced to class A if serious physical injury is inflicted or if the victim is a special victim.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for special victim

headings.title: Elements of assault in the third degree

headings.title: Elements of assault in the fourth degree

headings.title: Protection against disclosure of residence address by special victims
headings.reviewNote: Protects special victims from disclosing current residential address except in camera to the court for jurisdiction and venue determinations.

headings.reviewNote: Authorizes special victims to file assault petitions using identifying initials instead of legal names upon alleging endangerment from disclosure.

headings.reviewNote: Classifies fourth degree domestic assault as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony upon prior findings of guilt.

headings.title: Definitions of assault offenses and prior or persistent offenders
headings.reviewNote: Defines assault offense, persistent assault offender (two prior within ten years), and prior assault offender (one prior within five years).

headings.title: Mandatory minimum imprisonment and probation or parole restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits suspended imposition of sentence or fines in lieu of prison, requiring at least six months imprisonment before parole or probation eligibility.

headings.title: Pleading, proof, and judicial findings required for offender status
headings.reviewNote: Requires pleading essential facts, proof beyond a reasonable doubt, and judicial findings to establish prior or persistent assault offender status.

headings.title: Timing and hearing outside jury presence in jury trials
headings.reviewNote: Requires pleading, proving, and finding offender status prior to jury submission and outside the jury's hearing.

headings.title: Deferral of proof and findings in bench trials or guilty pleas
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to defer proof and findings of offender status until prior to sentencing in bench trials or guilty pleas.

headings.title: Rights of confrontation, cross-examination, and defense evidence
headings.reviewNote: Accords defendants full rights of confrontation, cross-examination, and presentation of evidence at offender status hearings.

headings.title: Waiver of proof of alleged facts by defendant
headings.reviewNote: Permits defendant to waive proof of alleged prior or persistent offender facts.

headings.title: Use of presentence investigations and commitments permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that provisions do not prevent the use of presentence investigations or commitments.

headings.title: Presentation of additional sentencing information by parties
headings.reviewNote: Permits both state and defendant to present additional information bearing on sentencing at the sentencing hearing.

headings.title: Prior guilt findings requirement before date of present offense
headings.reviewNote: Requires that predicate findings of guilt occurred prior to the date of commission of the charged offense.

headings.title: Exclusion of punishment instructions and jury sentencing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits instructing jury on punishment ranges or allowing jury assessment of punishment for prior or persistent assault offenders.

headings.title: Evidentiary hearing on prior convictions outside jury hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to hear and determine prior conviction evidence out of the jury's hearing, including highway patrol MULES records.

headings.title: Sentence enhancement of one felony class for prior assault offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates sentencing prior assault offenders convicted of class B, C, or D felonies to the authorized term for one class step higher.

headings.title: Sentence enhancement of two felony classes for persistent assault offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates sentencing persistent assault offenders to authorized terms two class steps higher for class C or D felonies, and class A for class B felonies.

headings.title: Law enforcement investigation exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities of federal, state, county, or municipal law enforcement officers conducting law enforcement investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, delayed effective date 7-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability/nonseverability notes; 7-01-27 version expanding prior enhancement predicates to include section 565.090 distinguished from 565.091:34707.

headings.title: Elements of masked intimidation
headings.reviewNote: Defines masked intimidation as intentionally harassing, intimidating, or threatening another while concealing face with intent to induce fear for physical safety.

headings.title: Graduated felony classifications for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Establishes graduated felony penalties: class E for first offense, class D for second, and class C for third or subsequent offenses.

headings.title: Exempted purposes for face coverings and protective masks
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates exemptions for masks worn for celebrations, workplace safety, weather, productions, emergency drills, health protection, or religion.

headings.title: Preservation of First Amendment constitutional rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that provisions shall not be construed to diminish or infringe upon rights protected under the First Amendment.

headings.title: Definitions of harass, intimidate, and threaten
headings.reviewNote: Defines statutory terms harass, intimidate (including civil rights interference based on protected status), and threaten.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections, L. 2026 S.B. 1421 history, and severability clause (§ 1.1010); masked intimidation elements, graduated class E/D/C felony penalties, 7 face-covering exemptions, First Amendment clause, and definitions verified.

headings.title: Elements and unlawful purposes of kidnapping in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines first degree kidnapping as unlawful removal or substantial confinement without consent for ransom, hostage, interference, felony, or terrorizing purposes.

headings.title: Classification and reduced felony class for certain purposes
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree kidnapping as a class A felony, reduced to class B felony if committed to facilitate a felony/flight or inflict injury/terrorize.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, effective date 1-01-17, Megan's Law cross-reference (589.400–589.426), and 3 case annotations (Stewart, Daleske, Phelps); five first-degree kidnapping purposes and class A/class B classifications verified.

headings.title: Elements of child kidnapping by non-relative
headings.reviewNote: Defines child kidnapping as non-relative within third degree knowingly removing or confining child under fourteen without parental or guardian consent.

headings.title: Affirmative defense of protecting child from welfare danger
headings.reviewNote: Establishes affirmative defense where person reasonably believed actions were necessary to preserve the child from danger to welfare.

headings.title: Class A felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies child kidnapping as a class A felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; non-relative child kidnapping elements (under age 14), welfare-protection affirmative defense, and class A felony classification verified.

headings.title: Elements of kidnapping in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines second degree kidnapping as knowingly restraining another unlawfully and without consent, substantially interfering with liberty and risking serious physical injury.

headings.title: Class D felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies kidnapping in the second degree as a class D felony.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 1-01-17; second-degree kidnapping elements (unlawful restraint risking serious physical injury) and class D felony classification verified.

headings.title: Elements of kidnapping in the third degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines third degree kidnapping as knowingly restraining another unlawfully and without consent so as to interfere substantially with liberty.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancement for out-of-state removal
headings.reviewNote: Classifies third degree kidnapping as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony if the person is removed from Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 1-01-17; third-degree kidnapping elements and class A misdemeanor / class E felony out-of-state removal enhancement verified.

headings.title: Defenses to third degree kidnapping of child under seventeen
headings.reviewNote: Provides defense to third degree kidnapping of child under seventeen based on parental consent or non-out-of-state assumption of control by a relative.

headings.title: Definition of relative
headings.reviewNote: Defines relative as parent, stepparent, ancestor, sibling, uncle, or aunt, including relationships established through marriage or adoption.

headings.title: Burden of injecting defense on defendant
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of injecting the issue of a defense under this section upon the defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; defenses to third-degree kidnapping of child under 17, definition of relative, and defendant burden to inject verified.

headings.title: Elements of interference with custody
headings.reviewNote: Defines interference with custody as knowingly and without legal right taking or enticing any person entrusted by court order to another's custody.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancement for removal or concealment
headings.reviewNote: Classifies interference with custody as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony if removed from Missouri, detained out-of-state, or concealed.

headings.title: Restitution for search and return expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to assess restitution against defendant for reasonable expenses incurred by custodian or parent in searching for or returning the child.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, effective date 1-01-17, and 1984 State v. Edmisten annotation; interference with custody elements, class A/class E removal or concealment enhancement, and permissive search/return restitution verified.

headings.title: Elements of parental kidnapping in absence of custody order
headings.reviewNote: Defines parental kidnapping as removing, detaining, concealing, or enticing away child without good cause and with intent to deprive another's custody rights.

headings.title: Graduated felony classifications based on detention duration
headings.reviewNote: Classifies parental kidnapping as class E felony, elevated to class D for 60 to 119 days concealment, and class B for 120 days or longer.

headings.title: Ineffectiveness of subsequent custody or visitation orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a subsequently obtained court order for custody or visitation does not affect the application of the section.

headings.title: Restitution for search and return expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes assessment of restitution for reasonable search and return expenses incurred by legal custodian or parent.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; parental kidnapping in absence of custody order, graduated class E/D/B felony durations, ineffectiveness of subsequent orders, and permissive restitution verified.

headings.title: Elements and prohibited acts of child abduction
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates acts constituting child abduction during pending domestic proceedings, visitation overstays, paid abduction, retention, or unauthorized relocation.

headings.title: Class E felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies child abduction as a class E felony.

headings.title: Restitution for search and return expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes assessment of restitution for reasonable expenses incurred in searching for or returning the child.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; five child abduction acts (including section 452.377 relocation), class E felony classification, and permissive search/return restitution verified.

headings.title: Temporary protective custody by peace officer upon risk of flight
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officer investigating custody interference, parental kidnapping, or abduction to take child into protective custody upon flight risk.

headings.title: Return of child to lawful custodian and protective exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Directs law enforcement officer to return child to lawful custodian unless good cause exists to retain temporary protective custody under section 210.125.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; permissive peace-officer temporary protective custody upon flight risk and mandatory return to lawful custodian absent section 210.125 good cause verified.

headings.title: Elements of abuse of elderly, disabled, or vulnerable person
headings.reviewNote: Defines abuse of an elderly, disabled, or vulnerable person through repeated emotional distress, intentional care failure, or creating substantial risk.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification and spiritual treatment exception
headings.reviewNote: Classifies abuse as class A misdemeanor and clarifies that reliance on spiritual healing through prayer does not constitute abuse.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 1-01-17; three elder/disabled/vulnerable-person abuse prongs, class A misdemeanor classification, and spiritual-treatment prayer exception verified.

headings.title: Elements of failure to report elder abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of failure to report elder abuse or neglect when a mandated reporter under section 192.2405 knowingly fails to report.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to report elder abuse or neglect as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 1-01-17; knowing failure to make mandated elder-abuse report under section 192.2405(1)(2) and class A misdemeanor classification verified.

headings.title: Elements of filing a false elder abuse or neglect report
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of filing a false elder abuse or neglect report as knowingly filing a false report.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancement for repeat offenders
headings.reviewNote: Classifies false reporting as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony upon prior findings of guilt for making false reports.

headings.title: Judicial hearing on prior findings of guilt outside jury presence
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to hear and determine evidence of prior false reporting findings of guilt outside the jury's hearing before submission.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; false elder abuse/neglect report elements, class A/class E repeat enhancement, and outside-jury judicial hearing on prior findings verified.

headings.title: Elements of failure to report vulnerable person abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of failure to report vulnerable person abuse or neglect when a mandated reporter under section 630.162 knowingly fails to report.

headings.title: Classification, fines, school fund deposit, and repeat felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to report as class A misdemeanor with fine up to $1,000, enhanced to class E felony and $5,000 fine for repeats, dedicated to schools.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date 1-01-17; knowing failure to report under section 630.162, class A ($1,000) / repeat class E ($5,000) penalties, and state school moneys fund transfer (sections 166.051/163.031) verified.

headings.title: Elements of filing a false vulnerable person abuse report
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of filing a false vulnerable person abuse report as knowingly filing a false report of abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Classification, fines, school fund deposit, and repeat felony enhancement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies false reporting as class A misdemeanor with fine up to $1,000, enhanced to class E felony and $5,000 fine for repeats, dedicated to schools.

headings.title: Judicial hearing on prior findings of guilt outside jury presence
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to hear and determine evidence of prior findings of guilt outside the jury's hearing prior to case submission.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; false vulnerable-person abuse report elements, class A ($1,000) / repeat class E ($5,000) penalties dedicated to public schools, and outside-jury prior-findings hearing verified.

headings.title: Definition of disturbs
headings.reviewNote: Defines disturbs as course of conduct serving no legitimate purpose causing a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or emotionally distressed.

headings.title: Elements and aggravating conditions of stalking in the first degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines first degree stalking as purposeful disturbing conduct accompanied by threats, order violations, age disparity, prior offenses, or address tampering.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest upon probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement officers to arrest without a warrant any person supported by probable cause of first degree stalking.

headings.title: Law enforcement investigation exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities of federal, state, county, or municipal law enforcement officers conducting official law enforcement investigations.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for repeat offenders or targeted officers
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree stalking as a class E felony, enhanced to class D for repeat stalking or targeting law enforcement personnel or family.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 5 subsections and Revisor's dual-version note; pre-2027 first-degree stalking version ('disturbs' definition plus 6 aggravating prongs) distinguished from restructured 7-01-27 version 565.225:60743.

headings.title: Elements of first degree stalking and technological abuse
headings.reviewNote: Defines first degree stalking through course of conduct or technological abuse inducing reasonable fear of harm, family harm, property harm, or terror (effective 7-01-27).

headings.title: Warrantless arrest upon probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement officers to arrest without a warrant any person supported by probable cause of first degree stalking.

headings.title: Law enforcement investigation exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities of federal, state, county, or municipal law enforcement officers conducting official law enforcement investigations.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for repeat offenders or targeted officers
headings.reviewNote: Classifies first degree stalking as a class E felony, enhanced to class D for repeat stalking or targeting law enforcement personnel or family (effective 7-01-27).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, delayed effective date 7-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability/nonseverability notes; refined subsection 1 title to highlight technological abuse and 4-prong reasonable-fear/harassment rewrite distinguishing it from 565.225:34708.

headings.title: Elements of stalking in the second degree
headings.reviewNote: Defines second degree stalking as purposely disturbing or following another person with intent to disturb through a course of conduct.

headings.title: Law enforcement investigation exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities of federal, state, county, or municipal law enforcement officers conducting official law enforcement investigations.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest upon probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement officers to arrest without a warrant any person supported by probable cause of second degree stalking.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for repeat offenders or targeted officers
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second degree stalking as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony for repeat stalking or targeting law enforcement personnel or family.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and Revisor's dual-version note; pre-2027 second-degree stalking version (purposeful disturbing course of conduct) distinguished from 7-01-27 version 565.227:60744.

headings.title: Elements of second degree stalking and technological abuse
headings.reviewNote: Defines second degree stalking as knowingly engaging in targeted course of conduct or technological abuse causing a reasonable person to feel harassed, terrified, or intimidated (effective 7-01-27).

headings.title: Law enforcement investigation exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities of federal, state, county, or municipal law enforcement officers conducting official law enforcement investigations.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest upon probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes law enforcement officers to arrest without a warrant any person supported by probable cause of second degree stalking.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for repeat offenders or targeted officers
headings.reviewNote: Classifies second degree stalking as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony for repeat stalking or targeting law enforcement personnel or family (effective 7-01-27).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, delayed effective date 7-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability/nonseverability notes; refined subsection 1 title and note to match knowing technological abuse and 'harassed, terrified, or intimidated' wording distinguishing it from 565.227:34709.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful posting of personally identifiable information online
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of knowingly posting personally identifiable information online intending or threatening to cause great bodily harm or death.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancements for protected officials or resulting harm
headings.reviewNote: Classifies online posting as class C misdemeanor, elevated to class E felony for protected justice officials/family, and class D felony if harm results.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, transfer note (formerly 578.450, eff. 1-01-17), and 2023 S.B. 103 amendment; online PII posting with intent/threat of great bodily harm or death and class C/E/D enhancements for justice officials and resulting harm verified.

headings.title: Elements of invasion of privacy
headings.reviewNote: Defines invasion of privacy as nonconsensual photography or recording of a person in nudity where privacy is expected or under/through clothing.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancements for dissemination, multiple victims, or repeats
headings.reviewNote: Classifies invasion of privacy as a class A misdemeanor, enhanced to class E felony upon distribution, dissemination, multiple victims, or prior conviction.

headings.title: Pleading and proof requirements for prior findings of guilt
headings.reviewNote: Requires prior findings of guilt to be pleaded and proven pursuant to the procedures set out in section 558.021.

headings.title: Definition of same course of conduct
headings.reviewNote: Defines same course of conduct as viewing, photographing, filming, or videotaping more than one person under similar circumstances pursuant to one scheme.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and effective date 1-01-17; invasion of privacy elements, class A/class E enhancements (distribution, dissemination, multiple victims, repeat), section 558.021 prior-proof rule, and 'same course of conduct' definition verified.

headings.title: Creation and composition of Stop Cyberstalking and Harassment Task Force
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Stop Cyberstalking and Harassment Task Force and specifies its legislative, executive, law enforcement, judicial, and public membership.

headings.title: Task force chairperson election, initial meeting, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Directs majority election of a chairperson, mandates an initial meeting before October 1, 2024, and authorizes reimbursement of actual meeting expenses.

headings.title: Stakeholder feedback collection on victim treatment and prevention
headings.reviewNote: Directs task force to gather stakeholder feedback to develop best practices for victim treatment and stopping cyberstalking and harassment.

headings.title: Mandatory study areas and legislative recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Charges task force with studying and recommending measures on law enforcement training, interagency coordination, forensic tools, and victim services.

headings.title: Administrative support by department of public safety
headings.reviewNote: Designates the department of public safety to provide administrative support to the task force.

headings.title: Annual reporting deadline to governor and general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires task force to submit an annual report of its findings to the governor and general assembly on or before December 31.

headings.title: Expiration date and administrative extension authorization
headings.reviewNote: Establishes task force expiration on December 31, 2026, permitting administrative extension by the department of public safety until December 31, 2028.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 7 subsections and L. 2024 S.B. 754 history; Stop Cyberstalking and Harassment Task Force membership, initial meeting before Oct 1, 2024, study/reporting duties, DPS support, and Dec 31, 2026 (extendable to Dec 31, 2028) expiration verified.

headings.title: Elements of unlawful tracking of a motor vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Defines unlawful tracking as placing an electronic tracking device on a motor vehicle without all owners' consent to monitor occupants, excluding manufacturers.

headings.title: Exempted tracking activities, parental monitoring, and commercial exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory exemptions for law enforcement, parents monitoring minors, stolen property recovery, guardians, rental fleets, lienholders, and insurance.

headings.title: Inapplicability to manufacturer-installed tracking systems
headings.reviewNote: Excludes manufacturer-installed vehicle tracking systems from statutory tracking prohibitions.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancement for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unlawful tracking as a class A misdemeanor for a first offense and a class E felony for repeat offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, delayed effective date 07-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability clause (§ 1.1005); unlawful motor vehicle tracking elements, 8 statutory exemptions, manufacturer exclusion, and class A/class E repeat penalties verified.

headings.title: Statutory title and citation as Infant's Protection Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates the section as the Infant's Protection Act.

headings.title: Definitions of born, living infant, and partially born
headings.reviewNote: Defines statutory terms born, living infant (under thirty days post birth), and partially born based on anatomical delivery landmarks.

headings.title: Elements of the offense of infanticide
headings.reviewNote: Defines infanticide as purposefully causing the death of a living infant through an overt act performed when the infant is born or partially born.

headings.title: Class A felony classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of infanticide as a class A felony.

headings.title: Medical life-saving exceptions and maternal nonresponsibility
headings.reviewNote: Excludes criminal responsibility for physicians performing customary life-saving procedures for mother or unborn/partially born child, and for mothers when the physician is not criminally responsible.

headings.title: Exemption for abortion acts performed prior to partial birth
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not apply to legal abortion acts performed prior to the child being partially born.

headings.title: Limitation of culpability to overt acts and substantial steps
headings.reviewNote: Limits criminal culpability to persons performing the overt act or taking a substantial step with purposeful intent resulting in infant death.

headings.title: Preservation of statutory criminal defenses
headings.reviewNote: Preserves general criminal responsibility and justification defenses provided under chapters 562 and 563.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 8 subsections, effective date 1-01-17, and 2 case annotations (2002 State v. RHS; 2004 RHS of Planned Parenthood v. Nixon holding section unconstitutional for lacking maternal health exception); refined subsection 5 title to 'maternal nonresponsibility'.

headings.title: Elements of cyberharassment through digital communications
headings.reviewNote: Defines cyberharassment as purposeful or knowing fear-inducing electronic conduct causing reasonable fear, anxiety, or terror by repeated contact without legitimate purpose.

headings.title: Classification and enhancement for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies cyberharassment as a class B misdemeanor for a first offense and a class A misdemeanor for second or subsequent offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, delayed effective date 7-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability/nonseverability notes; cyberharassment digital course-of-conduct elements and class B/class A repeat misdemeanor classifications verified.

headings.title: Elements of cyberstalking using electronic devices
headings.reviewNote: Defines cyberstalking as purposeful or knowing electronic conduct enhancing the ability to intimidate, track, follow, or induce reasonable fear or terror.

headings.title: Classification and felony enhancement for repeat offenses
headings.reviewNote: Classifies cyberstalking as a class A misdemeanor for a first offense and a class E felony for second or subsequent offenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, delayed effective date 7-01-27 (§ 565.019), and severability/nonseverability notes; cyberstalking electronic-device elements and class A misdemeanor / class E repeat felony classifications verified.
